content: The following studies and clinical trials have investigated the effects of acupuncture and related therapies on chronic low back pain: 1. A 2013 randomized, patient-assessor-blinded, sham-controlled clinical trial evaluated the effects of auricular acupuncture on chronic pain in adults with back musculoskeletal disorders. The study was conducted by de Castro Moura et al. 2. A 2019 study by Kim et al. demonstrated that reduced tactile acuity in chronic low back pain is associated with structural neuroplasticity in the primary somatosensory cortex. This neuroplasticity was shown to be modulated by acupuncture therapy. 3. Kong et al. (2020) conducted a randomized clinical trial comparing electroacupuncture to sham treatment in adults with chronic low back pain. The study assessed changes in pain severity and found significant differences favoring electroacupuncture. 4. Ushinohama et al. (2016) investigated the effects of a single session of ear acupuncture on pain intensity and postural control in individuals with chronic low back pain. This was a randomized controlled trial. 5. Molsberger et al. (2002) conducted a randomized, blinded, controlled trial with a three-month follow-up to determine whether acupuncture improves orthopedic management of chronic low back pain. 6. Martín-Corrales et al. (2020) explored the benefits of adding gluteal dry needling to a four-week physical exercise program in patients with chronic low back pain. This was a randomized clinical trial. 7. Koppenhaver et al. (2021) examined the effect of dry needling on lumbar muscle stiffness in patients with low back pain. This double-blind, randomized controlled trial utilized shear wave elastography for assessment. 8. Kerr et al. (2003) conducted a blinded randomized controlled trial to evaluate acupuncture's role in managing chronic low back pain. 9. The German Acupuncture Trials (GERAC) in 2007 involved a randomized, multicenter, blinded, parallel-group trial with three groups to assess acupuncture's efficacy for chronic low back pain. 10. Huang et al. (2019) conducted a randomized controlled sham acupuncture trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for chronic discogenic sciatica. 11. Brinkhaus et al. (2006) performed a randomized controlled trial to assess acupuncture's effects on patients with chronic low back pain. 12. Cherkin et al. (2009) compared acupuncture, simulated acupuncture, and usual care in a randomized trial for chronic low back pain. 13. Cho et al. (2013) conducted a multicenter, randomized, patient-assessor-blinded, sham-controlled clinical trial to evaluate acupuncture for chronic low back pain. 14. De Castro Moura et al. (2019) studied the effects of auricular acupuncture on chronic pain in adults with back musculoskeletal disorders in a randomized clinical trial. 15. Yuan et al. (2016) reported minor adverse events such as transient worsening of back pain, acupuncture point pain, bruising, and discomfort in a study on acupuncture for chronic nonspecific low back pain. 16. Meng et al. (2003) investigated acupuncture combined with electrical stimulation for chronic low back pain in older patients in a randomized controlled trial. 17. Moslemi and Farokhi (2020) examined the effects of electroacupuncture on pain, functional disability, and ultrasonographic changes in the gluteus maximus muscle in patients with nonspecific chronic low back pain. 18. Pan et al. (2019) conducted a clinical trial on acupuncture combined with sling exercise training for lumbar disc herniation. 19. Ren et al. (2021) studied the analgesic effects of acupuncture based on meridian-tendon dialectical theory in chronic low back pain. 20. Sung et al. (2020) evaluated the efficacy and safety of thread embedding acupuncture combined with traditional acupuncture for chronic low back pain in a randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded, multicenter clinical trial. 21. Tabatabaiee et al. (2019) demonstrated that ultrasound-guided dry needling reduces pain in patients with piriformis syndrome. 22. Wang et al. (2020) investigated the effects of acupuncture combined with fire acupuncture on pain and serum inflammatory factors in patients with lumbar disc herniation. 23. Yeung et al. (2003) studied the use of electroacupuncture in conjunction with exercise for chronic low back pain treatment. 24. Zaringhalam et al. (2010) conducted a randomized controlled clinical trial on acupuncture and baclofen for reducing chronic nonspecific low back pain. 25. Zhai and Wang (2019) explored the therapeutic effects of drug cupping combined with deep puncture on Jiaji points for lumbar disc herniation. 26. Zhu (2021) conducted a clinical trial on warming-needle moxibustion combined with joint loosening for chronic low back pain. 27. Yuan et al. (2016) performed a clinical trial on acupuncture therapy for chronic nonspecific low back pain. 28. Molsberger et al. (2002) evaluated acupuncture's role in orthopedic management of chronic low back pain in a randomized, blinded, controlled trial with a three-month follow-up. 29. Brinkhaus et al. (2006) conducted a randomized controlled trial on acupuncture for chronic low back pain. These studies collectively highlight the potential benefits of acupuncture and related therapies in managing chronic low back pain, with varying levels of evidence and methodological rigor.
